chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from a man whom he named Sawadah, who said:

We were a group at Mina, and the sacrificial animals had become scarce. So we looked, and there was Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام standing by the flock, bargaining for sheep and haggling with them intensely, while we were waiting.
When he had finished, he turned toward us and said: I think you were surprised by my haggling. We said: Yes. He said: Indeed, the one who is cheated is neither praised nor rewarded.

Do you have some need? We said: Yes, may Allah set you aright; the sacrificial animals have become too costly for us. He said: Gather together and buy a camel, then sacrifice it among yourselves. We said: Our means do not reach that. He said: Then gather together and buy a cow among yourselves. We said: Our means still do not reach that either. He said: Then gather together and buy a sheep and slaughter it among yourselves. We said: Will it suffice for seven? He said: Yes, and for seventy.

key_terms.الْأَضَاحِيُّ: the sacrificial animals offered in hajj or 'Id sacrifice
key_terms.الْمَغْبُونَ: the one who is financially taken advantage of in a transaction
key_terms.بَقَرَةً: a cow used as sacrificial livestock
key_terms.تُجْزِي: it suffices or is legally valid on behalf of
key_terms.مِكَاسِي: my bargaining or haggling in purchase

ai.seo_question: Can one sheep suffice as a shared sacrifice for multiple people at Mina according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a ruling concerning shared udhiyah at Mina when sacrificial animals become expensive or scarce. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام permits a group to jointly purchase and sacrifice even a single sheep, affirming that it may suffice not only for seven but even for seventy people.
